azores.intro: São Miguel's great trees are imports that found a home, Moreton Bay Figs from Australia, Norfolk Island Pines from the Pacific, a pohutukawa from New Zealand and a coast redwood, planted in the island's squares and gardens. In Ponta Delgada the pohutukawa of the Campo de São Francisco, classified in 1965, is by local accounts the first tree the Azores protected, and the Jardim António Borges keeps a colossal fig. In Furnas a Norfolk Island Pine found by chance in 2010 rises 50 metres above the lake.
azores.meta_description: Seven remarkable trees on São Miguel, Azores: Ponta Delgada's pohutukawa and giant figs, and the 50-metre Norfolk Island Pine of Furnas, and how to visit.
azores.question_meta: São Miguel's best-known trees are Ponta Delgada's pohutukawa and Moreton Bay Figs and the Norfolk Island Pines of Furnas.
azores.question_answer: The remarkable trees of the Azores are on São Miguel, in Ponta Delgada and Furnas. In Ponta Delgada, the pohutukawa of the Campo de São Francisco was classified in 1965, by local accounts the first protected tree in the islands; the Jardim António Borges has a colossal Moreton Bay Fig and a Norfolk Island Pine, and a fig by the Jardim José do Canto came second in Portugal's Tree of the Year 2026. In Furnas, about 40 km east, a Norfolk Island Pine 50 metres tall stands on the lakeshore, with a classified redwood and Terra Nostra's Lady of the Park nearby.
azores.question_context: Locally the figs are called Australian rubber trees; botanists know them as Moreton Bay Figs, Ficus macrophylla. The Jardim António Borges was laid out between 1858 and 1861, belongs to Ponta Delgada's council and is free; its fig and its Norfolk Island Pine stand about 130 metres apart, and no source dates either to the first planting. Nothing on record ties the Tree of the Year runner-up to one trunk, so its pin follows the tree mapped under the contest's name. The pohutukawa is put at 125 to 150 years by two local estimates, and its crown has rested on steel props and cables since work in 2013. In Furnas, the lakeshore pine was found during clearing work in 2010 and given as 50.10 metres tall; it is free to see on the signed PRC06SMI lake walk. Terra Nostra's figures for the Lady of the Park, 52 metres and about 200 years, are the park's own. The redwood stands inside the ticketed Mata-Jardim José do Canto, and the register records no size or age for it.

faq.q: Which Azores tree was in Portugal's Tree of the Year?
faq.a: Two were entered in 2026. The Australian rubber tree of Ponta Delgada, a Moreton Bay Fig by the Jardim José do Canto, finished second behind the cedar of Runa. Parque Terra Nostra also entered its Norfolk Island Pine, the Lady of the Park.

faq.q: Is the Jardim António Borges free?
faq.a: Yes, it is a municipal garden owned by Ponta Delgada's council, about ten minutes on foot from the Portas da Cidade. It holds both the colossal Moreton Bay Fig and a Norfolk Island Pine near the small lake.

faq.q: Can you see the giant Norfolk Island Pine at Lagoa das Furnas for free?
faq.a: Yes. It stands on public ground on the lake's south shore, beside the Furnas interpretation centre, with an information board next to it, on the signed PRC06SMI lake walk. The classified redwood nearby is inside the Mata-Jardim José do Canto, which charges 5 euros from age 13.

angra-do-heroismo.intro: Two trees protected by the Azores stand in parishes just outside Angra do Heroísmo, on Terceira, rather than in its historic centre. In Posto Santo, about four kilometres north, a cork oak classified in 1985 grows in the church square, and a summary of its decree calls it the only cork oak on the island. In Terra Chã, about three kilometres west, a til, a laurel at home in Madeira and the Canaries, has been a tree of public interest since 1966. Each is about ten minutes from the centre by car.
angra-do-heroismo.meta_description: Two protected trees near Angra do Heroísmo, Terceira: the cork oak of Posto Santo and the til of Terra Chã, where they stand and how to reach them.
angra-do-heroismo.question_meta: Near Angra do Heroísmo, Terceira, two protected trees stand outside the centre, a cork oak in Posto Santo and a til in Terra Chã.
angra-do-heroismo.question_answer: Two protected trees near Angra do Heroísmo are worth the short trip out of the centre. The cork oak in the church square of Posto Santo, about 4 km north, was classified in 1985, and a summary of its decree calls it the only cork oak on Terceira. The til of Terra Chã, about 3 km west on Canada de Belém, has been a tree of public interest since 1966. Each is roughly ten minutes from the centre by car or taxi.
angra-do-heroismo.question_context: Neither tree is in Angra's historic centre, and bus connections to Posto Santo and Terra Chã have not been checked, so plan on a car or a taxi. The cork oak is classified of municipal interest under a regional decree of May 1985, confirmed in the Azores' 2015 list; by the decree's description it stands between the parish church and the parish council building, and it can be seen for free from the square. The decree's full text could not be read, so its claim that this is the island's only cork oak is reported, not checked. The til is classified of public interest, by an order of July 1966; a 2006 photograph captioned at Terra Chã gives 1965. Its pin is approximate, taken from Street View in 2020, which suggests it stands by the road; whether it grows on private ground behind a wall is not established, so look from the road. Neither tree has a published girth, height or age, and neither has a dated sighting from recent years. A photograph from either spot would settle that.

faq.q: Are these trees in Angra's historic centre?
faq.a: No. The cork oak is in the church square of Posto Santo, about 4 km north, and the til is on Canada de Belém in Terra Chã, about 3 km west. Each is about ten minutes from the centre by car or taxi.

faq.q: Is the Posto Santo cork oak the only one on Terceira?
faq.a: That is how a summary of its 1985 decree describes it. The decree's full text could not be read to confirm the wording, so treat it as the decree's claim.

faq.q: Can you visit the til of Terra Chã?
faq.a: It appears to stand by the public road on Canada de Belém, but its pin is approximate and it may grow on private ground behind a wall, so see it from the road.
